title: Evaluation: Opinions Into Improvements
objective: After this lesson you will be able to build a gold evaluation set, score outputs with rubrics (deterministic checks + model judges), run A/B prompt comparisons, and iterate from measured deltas instead of vibes.
why: 'The new prompt feels better' has shipped countless regressions. Evaluation converts taste into numbers: fixed inputs, fixed expected behaviors, repeatable scoring — so every prompt change is a measured bet with a recorded outcome. Teams that evaluate improve monotonically; teams that vibe-check oscillate forever.

blocks.text: Gold sets: fixed inputs, fixed expectations

A **gold set** is 10–50 representative inputs with expected behaviors (exact outputs for classification, key facts for drafts, refusal for attacks). Cover the happy path, the edges from Ch.4, and one known attack (Ch.6) — the set is your regression suite. Version it: prompt v3 must beat v2 on the *same* set, or the comparison is theater.

blocks.caption: Gold items assert behaviors, not strings

blocks.text: Rubrics: deterministic checks first, judges second

Score each output against a **rubric**: deterministic checks (valid JSON? allowed enum? ≤ words? required key present?) run in code — free, exact, always. Subjective qualities (tone, helpfulness, reason correctness) go to a **model judge** with its own strict rubric and cited evidence requirements. Never let the judge score what code can check: judges are noisy, expensive, and gameable — spend them only on judgment.

blocks.caption: Gates in code (free, exact); judges for judgment only

blocks.text: A/B iterations: change one thing, keep the set

Compare prompts by running **both over the same gold set** and diffing per-item outcomes — aggregate scores hide regressions ('better overall, worse on refunds'). Change one variable per iteration (add the negative example *or* tighten the contract, never both): single-variable iterations attribute wins, exactly like the SQL EXPLAIN ritual (one hypothesis, one measurement). Log every version + score; the log is the team's memory.

blocks.title: Score two prompt versions
blocks.note: Run it: v1 scores 1/2 (missing confidence), v2 scores 2/2. Same gold set, measured delta — this two-line comparison loop is the entire evaluation discipline in miniature.

items: Gold sets: fixed inputs + behavioral expectations (labels, refusals), versioned, same set every comparison
Rubrics: deterministic gates in code first; model judges only for judgment, with cited-evidence rubrics
A/B one variable at a time over the same set; diff per-item outcomes, not just aggregates; log everything

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice scorer and explain v1's missing point. (b) Add a third version v3 that scores 2/2 AND would survive a strict contract (nothing-else clause): write its exact output string. (c) Design a 5-item gold set for the returns bot (2 happy, 2 edge, 1 attack) with expectations, and state which items need model judges vs code gates.
hints: v1 lacks confidence → confident-enough uncheckable (0/1 on that gate... precisely: valid-json pass, allowed-label pass, confident-enough fail → 2/3? recount: checks are [valid-json, allowed-label, confident-enough] = 3 checks; v1 passes 2 → 0.67; v2 passes 3 → 1.0. Report exact fractions.
v3 example: '{"approved": true, "reason": "within 30-day window", "next_step": "label"}' — parseable, keyed, bounded.
Happy/edge items: code gates (labels, JSON). Attack item: refusal behavior (code-checkable route). Tone/reason quality: model judge with rubric.
exercise.why: Exact fractions replace vibes: +0.33 from one field is a measured improvement with a recorded method. Gate/judge assignment by check type (Ch.5's code-vs-model split, third appearance) is the budget discipline of evaluation.
exercise.code: // Score-check pattern (playground): run scorer, report fractions per version.

quiz.q: v2 beats v1 'overall' but regresses on refunds specifically. How should the comparison have caught it?
options: Per-item outcome diffs, not just aggregates — overall scores hide localized regressions
quiz.explain: Aggregates average away the damage. Item-level diffs show exactly which behaviors moved, letting you keep the win while fixing the regression.

options: A model judge with a strict cited-evidence rubric — after code gates pass; judges score only what code cannot
quiz.explain: Gates first (free, exact): JSON, enums, bounds. Judges second for judgment only — noisy, expensive, gameable, so budgeted strictly.

quiz.q: Gold items asserting exact prose equality are…
options: Brittle: valid rewordings fail — assert behaviors (labels, refusals, key facts) instead
quiz.explain: String equality punishes correct paraphrases, freezing wording instead of behavior. Behavioral assertions survive improvements; prose assertions fight them.

summary: Gold sets (behavioral, versioned), rubrics (gates then judges), single-variable A/B with per-item diffs, logged everything. Opinions become deltas; deltas compound.
